blogs.title: Beyond the Classic Triad: Unmasking Telomere Biology Disorders in Adults with Pancytopenia and Fibrosis
blogs.description: In this post we review a young woman whose fatigue, anemia, hepatic and pulmonary fibrosis, and premature greying cast a wide net for diagnosis. We outline the atypical presentations of dyskeratosis congenita/TBD when mucocutaneous features are absent, review key red‑flags (cytopenia with ineffective erythropoiesis, organ fibrosis), and provide a pragmatic diagnostic algorithm that incorporates telomere length testing, second‑line imaging, and multidisciplinary referral.

blogs.title: Morphology Matters: Distinguishing Ineffective Erythropoiesis from Hemolytic Anemia in the Setting of Vitamin B12 Deficiency
blogs.description: The clinical picture of severe anemia can confound the work‑up. Here we discuss the classic peripheral smear findings—dimorphic red cells, basophilic stippling, Cabot rings and hypersegmented neutrophils—and how they differ from classic haemolysis. Discovery of a positive DAT, but lack of reticulocytosis and marrow hyperplasia, points toward ineffective erythropoiesis. We walk through the step‑by‑step approach to ruling out autoimmune hemolytic anemia versus B12‑deficiency‑driven marrow failure.

blogs.title: Variant of Uncertain Significance: How to Translate a Monoallelic PARN Missense Variant into Clinical Practice
blogs.description: A missense PARN variant (c.613T>C, p.Cys205Arg) flagged as VUS can feel like a clinical standstill. This post explains how to evaluate such a find using ACMG scoring, functional predictions, domain relevance, and phenotypic match. We cover inheritance nuances, family testing, and counseling strategies, and outline when to consider additional functional assays or re‑analysis as new data accumulates.

blogs.title: PARN Mutations: An Emerging Bridge Between Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis and Bone Marrow Failure
blogs.description: While most clinicians think of TERT and TERC in IPF, PARN is rising on that list. We dissect the literature, summarizing how monoallelic PARN variants are now linked to IPF, hepatic fibrosis, and hematologic compromise. The post offers a surveillance blueprint—from baseline pulmonary function and CT, to telomere length monitoring, to timely referral for lung transplantation—and discusses the interplay between the lung and bone marrow in telomere‑mediated disease.

blogs.title: Navigating The Management of Telomere Biology Disorders: From Supportive Care to Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant
blogs.description: Telomere biology disorders can spare or overwhelm multiple systems. In this article we lay out the current therapeutic armamentarium—nutritional correction, infection prophylaxis, anti‑androgens, bone marrow transplant candidacy, organ transplantation—and provide evidence‑based guidance on when to initiate aggressive therapy versus watchful waiting. We also examine psychosocial and genetic counseling considerations crucial for long‑term survivorship.
